About us

Activity

Whether you're training for your first 5K, getting back into it after a break or simply seeking a fun way to stay active, there's something to suit every level here, from yoga sessions to gym classes, team sports to outdoor adventures. Continue scrolling down to explore the options and make comparisons about what's in your budget and schedule and select the one that feels right for you this week.
You may be looking for something different or coming back to fitness after a hiatus; we've picked a few of the welcoming options, so you can get started with confidence.

Yoga: Soothing, relaxing classes designed for all levels of experience, novices to years of practice. Slow down, concentrate on your breathing and leave feeling relaxed than when you came.

Gym: Strengthen and enhance fitness in a progressive manner – offers equipment for increases and access to cardio equipment – staff are available to assist in creating a fitness plan suited to your needs and abilities.

Team Sports: Make friends and stay active together with football, netball, basketball and other casual sports. Choose a group where you feel comfortable and have fun playing in a team.

Fresh Air: For fresh air, parks, trails and open air sessions are in the neighborhood. Walking spaces or outdoor fitness circuits, there is room to get active no matter the weather.

We'll describe what the activity entails, the level of difficulty (beginner, medium or advanced), activity timings, what to bring and what to expect on your first visit.

Price & Memberships

Price & Memberships: Don't let your activity costs go out of control. We clearly display price ranges so you can quickly understand your price range.

Pay as you go: No obligation. Simply show up, pay for the session and go, whenever you want for the week.

Student deals and discounts: Discounted gym memberships, class passes and more for students at the University of Hertfordshire. Show your student ID to see what you can save.

Monthly memberships: This is best if you plan to attend regularly and have a monthly plan to help you maintain your sessions without paying per session.

Free trial sessions: Give it a test drive, and determine if it's the right fit before you make any investment.

Location & Timings

Activities by Location & Timings: It's easy to find activities near where you live, study or work and plan your visit with all the info.

Map view: At a single glance discover what is near you, gyms, studios, parks, sport pitches and so much more, so that you can choose what is closest.

Address and hours: All venues have complete addresses and hours, so you can be sure to know where to go & when to arrive.

Class timetables: Make sure to identify a class time that works for you that may be early in the morning, between classes or late at night.

Accessibility information: Ensure step-free access, changing facilities and other information are provided to ensure everyone can participate in an easy-to-handicap way.

Travel and parking information: Get up to date information on getting there by bus, train, bike, walking and parking.

Top Rated & Recommended

Top Rated & Recommended: if you're not sure where to begin? Have a look at the most popular and best rated activities. They're an excellent way to get started, and they are the types of exercises that we strongly suggest to anyone who is new to exercising.

Most popular activities: Find out which classes, gym and outdoor areas are fully booked at the moment, whether it's a lively community session or from a local favourite.

Highest rated: Check the locations that are best known for their welcoming staff, clean facilities and wonderful atmosphere to train in so you can train in a location you'll love!

New places and sessions are added regularly and you will never run out of “new things”.

Honest feedback from the community: Learn what to anticipate from a first visit, and which exercises are best for novices.

item.title: Our Story
item.dc:creator: ti25aai
item.content:encoded:
ActiveHeartz started with a simple problem. When we arrived at the University of Hertfordshire, we wanted to stay active, but we had no idea where to go. Which gyms do student prices? Where can you go for a run that isn't next to a main road? Is there anywhere to play football if you're not on a team?

The answers were spread across dozens of websites, leaflets and word of mouth. So we decided to put them all in one place, written by students, for students.

Who we made it for

ActiveHeartz is for anyone studying at the University of Hertfordshire, whether you live on campus, in Hatfield, or commute in. We especially had these people in mind:

  • First-years who are new to the area and don't know where anything is yet
  • Students on a tight budget who need free or cheap ways to stay fit
  • International students looking for a friendly way to settle in and meet people
  • Beginners who feel nervous walking into a gym or joining a team
  • Busy students juggling lectures, part-time work and deadlines

How we organise the site

We grouped everything so you can find what you need in a couple of clicks. Choose a section from the menu, then pick a place to read our review.

Parks

Free green spaces and trails for walking, running and cycling.

Gyms

Student-friendly gyms, pools and leisure centres.

Sports

Team sports and casual sessions where you can make friends.

Classes

Yoga, group classes and support for your wellbeing.

Deals

Student discounts, pay-as-you-go and free activities.

Getting there

Every review explains how to reach the place from campus.

How we review places

Every review on ActiveHeartz follows the same simple format, so you can compare places easily:

  • What it's like: an honest overview of what to expect on your first visit
  • Star rating: we only recommend places we would happily send a friend to
  • Cost: free, pay-as-you-go or membership, so you know what fits your budget
  • Getting there: walking, cycling, shuttle or bus routes from College Lane and de Havilland

We keep our reviews positive and responsible. Our aim is to help you find somewhere great to get active, not to criticise local businesses.

Why it matters to us

Moving more is one of the easiest ways to feel better, both physically and mentally. A walk between lectures, a swim after a long day or a weekly game with friends can make student life less stressful and a lot more fun. We hope ActiveHeartz helps you find your thing.

You don't need to be experienced or super fit to start. Just pick one thing to try this week.

Team contribution:

Biwon and Mirab (Researchers and writers) - We were in charge of making the website's content all the information and researching them to see which could suit the students this includes all the reviews, gyms, activities and all the information was written by us.

Tayyab and Haris (Main website developers) - we were in charge of making the website from scratch this includes the pictures, headings, navigation system and overall giving the website a cleaner look so it can be easy to find the information which was written.

item.title: Contact us
item.dc:creator: ti25aai
item.content:encoded:
Get in touch

Hi! We're a small group of University of Hertfordshire students who put ActiveHeartz together because we know how hard it can be to find somewhere to get active when you're new to the area, short on time or short on money.

If you've got a question, spotted something we've got wrong, or there's a park, gym or club you love that we haven't covered yet, we'd genuinely like to hear from you. Here's how to get hold of us.

Things people often message us about

  • Suggesting a place for us to review
  • Updating opening times or prices that have changed
  • Asking which activity might suit them as a beginner
  • Telling us about a student deal we've missed

How to reach us

  • Leave a comment under any of our reviews and one of us will reply there
  • Tell us which place your message is about, so we can find it quickly
  • If you are suggesting somewhere new, let us know where it is and what you liked about it
  • Please don't share personal details like your phone number or address in a comment

We're students too, so we check messages around lectures. We'll do our best to reply within a few days.

Need support right now? We're not able to give medical or mental health advice. If you're struggling, the University's Student Wellbeing team is there for you, and in an emergency always call 999.

item.title: Privacy Policy
item.dc:creator: ti25aai
item.content:encoded:
Who we are
ActiveHeartz (https://activeheartz.blog) is a student project made by University of Hertfordshire students. It recommends places to stay active and look after your wellbeing near the University.

What information we collect
We only collect what is needed for the site to work:

  • Comments: if you leave a comment, we collect the name and email address you enter, plus your IP address to help stop spam.
  • Site statistics: WordPress.com collects anonymous visitor statistics, such as which pages are viewed, to help us improve the site.

We never sell your information or use it for advertising.

Cookies
When you first visit, our cookie banner asks for your consent. Non-essential cookies, like those used for visitor statistics, are only used once you accept.

  • Essential cookies keep the site working, e.g. remembering that you entered the page password.
  • Comment cookies (optional) can remember your name and email for next time. These last one year.

You can clear cookies at any time in your browser settings.

Images and links to other websites
Our photos are free stock images. Some reviews link to official websites, such as leisure centres. Those websites have their own privacy policies, and we are not responsible for how they use your data.

How long we keep your data
Comments are kept so we can reply to them and stop spam. You can ask us to remove your comment at any time.

Your rights
Under GDPR, you can ask to see the personal data we hold about you, or ask us to delete it. To do this, leave a comment on any review and we will get back to you.

Changes to this policy
We may update this policy as the site develops. The latest version will always be on this page.

item.title: A Peaceful Walk at Ellenbrook Fields
item.dc:creator: ti25aai
item.content:encoded:
Ellenbrook Fields is a large, open country park on the edge of Hatfield, just a short walk from the de Havilland campus. It’s perfect for clearing your head between lectures, with wide grassy paths, wildflower meadows and plenty of space to walk, jog or cycle.

It’s free to visit and great for all fitness levels, whether you want a relaxed stroll or a steady run. It also hosts a free weekly parkrun, a friendly way to meet people and stay consistent.

Review by: Ethan Williams

Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (5/5)
Advantage: Beautiful open views, quiet surroundings and plenty of space for outdoor activities.

Disadvantage: The paths can be slippery in winter, and there are few sheltered areas.

Overall: Ellenbrook Fields is a fantastic place to spend time outdoors. It offers a relaxing environment away from busy roads and is ideal for long walks, jogging and spending time with dogs. The open fields make it enjoyable for people of different fitness levels.

Good to know

  • There are several entrances, including one close to the de Havilland campus
  • Paths are mostly flat, so it suits all fitness levels
  • Look out for wildflowers and skylarks in spring and summer
  • Our top tip: go at sunset for amazing big-sky views

Reviewed by Tayyib

item.title: Walk or Cycle the Alban Way
item.dc:creator: ti25aai
item.content:encoded:
The Alban Way is a traffic-free path that follows an old railway line between Hatfield and St Albans. It is flat, easy to follow and passes close to the University, so you can start a walk, run or bike ride almost from your front door.

Why we recommend it

  • Flat and traffic-free, so it is great for beginners and cyclists
  • Surrounded by trees and nature, a calm break from studying
  • Links Hatfield to St Albans, so you can make it a day out

Quick info

  • Review by: Daniel Johnson
  • Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⯪(4.5/5)
  • Advantage: good connection between Hatfield and St Albans
  • Disadvantage: Limited parking and no public toilets directly on the trail.
  • Overall: Its good because mainly its free so wont affect students and it is suitable for different fitness levels.
  • Level: Beginner

Good to know

  • The surface is mostly smooth, so it works for bikes and walkers
  • There are several access points, so you can do as much or as little as you like
  • You will pass old railway features along the way
  • Our top tip: cycle to St Albans and reward yourself with lunch in town
Visit website

Reviewed by the ActiveHeartz team

item.title: Lakeside Walks and Water Sports at Stanborough Park
item.dc:creator: ti25aai
item.content:encoded:
Stanborough Park in Welwyn Garden City is built around two lakes. You can enjoy an easy lakeside walk or jog, or try something different on the water at the park's water sports centre.

Why we recommend it

  • Beautiful lakeside paths for walking and running
  • Water sports like sailing and paddleboarding to try something new
  • Lots of open space for picnics and relaxing with friends

Quick info

  • Review by: Noah Davies
  • Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (5/5)
  • Advantage: Plenty of green space, scenic lake views and areas to sit and relax
  • Disadvantage: Some areas can be noisy and crowded during busy periods.
    Overall: Stanborough Park is a nice place to escape from everyday life and enjoy some fresh air. The lakeside setting makes it a good location for relaxing walks, picnics and spending time outdoors.

Good to know

  • There are paths around both lakes, so you can choose a short or long loop
  • Water sports are seasonal, so check what is running before you go
  • It is a popular spot for families on sunny weekends
  • Our top tip: go on a weekday afternoon for a quieter lakeside walk
Water sports centre

Reviewed by the ActiveHeartz team

item.title: A Run Around Historic Verulamium Park
item.dc:creator: ti25aai
item.content:encoded:
Verulamium Park in St Albans is one of the most popular parks in Hertfordshire. Wide paths loop around a lake and across open fields, with Roman ruins along the way, making every run or walk feel like a mini adventure.

Why we recommend it

  • Big, open park with lots of easy loops for running
  • Lake views and Roman history make it interesting to explore
  • Cafés and St Albans city centre close by

Quick info

  • Review by: Oliver Thomas
  • Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (5/5)
  • Advantage: Spacious parkland, attractive river views and interesting historical landmarks.
  • Disadvantage: Some walking routes can be muddy and uneven after rainfall.
  • Overall: Verulamium Park is an enjoyable destination for anyone who likes exploring the outdoors. It has a great mix of open fields, wildlife and historical attractions, making every visit interesting.

Good to know

  • The park is close to St Albans city centre and its cafés
  • You can see Roman remains as you walk around
  • The lake loop is a popular running route
  • Our top tip: pair your run with a visit to the city centre market
Visit website

Reviewed by the ActiveHeartz team

item.title: Gosling Sports Park: Something for Everyone
item.dc:creator: ti25aai
item.content:encoded:
Gosling Sports Park in Welwyn Garden City is a large sports centre with a gym, an athletics track, courts and pitches. Whether you want to lift weights, play tennis or try something more adventurous, it is all in one place.

Why we recommend it

  • Huge range of sports and activities on one site
  • Modern gym with plenty of equipment
  • Great for groups of friends wanting to try new sports

Quick info

  • Review by: James Walker
  • Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐ (4/5)
  • Advantage: A good variety of indoor and outdoor sports facilities, with activities for different skill levels.
  • Disadvantage: Booking certain activities can be difficult during busy periods, and some sessions may be expensive.
  • Overall: Gosling Sports Park is a useful place for people who enjoy staying fit and learning new skills. There are different activities to choose from, making it suitable for beginners as well as experienced sports players.

Good to know

  • There is a wide range of activities on one site
  • Some activities need booking, so plan ahead
  • There is parking on site if you are driving
  • Our top tip: check the timetable for quieter off-peak times
Visit website

Reviewed by the ActiveHeartz team

item.title: Make a Splash at Hatfield Swim Centre
item.dc:creator: ti25aai
item.content:encoded:
Hatfield Swim Centre is a modern pool and gym in Hatfield town. It is a convenient choice for students who want to swim laps, take it easy in the water or add a gym session to their week.

Why we recommend it

  • Clean, modern pool close to College Lane campus
  • Gym on site, so you can combine swimming and training
  • Flexible options with no long contract

Quick info

  • Review by: Lucas Harris
  • Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐ (4/5)
  • Advantage: Clean swimming pools, friendly atmosphere and a good choice of swimming sessions.
  • Disadvantage: Changing rooms can get busy, particularly during family swimming sessions.
  • Overall: Hatfield Swim Centre is an enjoyable place to spend time while keeping fit. It provides a good environment for practising swimming, building confidence in the water and learning new techniques.

Good to know

  • Lane sessions are usually split by speed
  • There is also a gym, so you can combine a swim with a workout
  • Off-peak times are usually calmer
  • Our top tip: bring a padlock for the lockers just in case
Visit website

Reviewed by the ActiveHeartz team

item.title: Hertfordshire Sports Village: Your Campus Gym
item.dc:creator: ti25aai
item.content:encoded:
The Hertfordshire Sports Village is the University's own sports centre on the de Havilland campus. It has a gym, swimming pool, sports halls and even a climbing wall, all just a few minutes from your lectures.

Why we recommend it

  • On campus, so it fits easily around your timetable
  • Student memberships designed for UH students
  • Gym, pool, sports halls and a climbing wall in one place

Quick info

  • Review by: Harry Clarke
  • Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (5/5)
  • Advantage: A wide range of sports facilities, fitness classes and opportunities to take part in team activities.
  • Disadvantage: The centre can feel busy at popular times, and finding parking may sometimes be difficult.
  • Overall: Hertfordshire Sports Village is a good destination for anyone looking to enjoy an active lifestyle. There are plenty of ways to exercise, improve sporting abilities and meet new people.

Good to know

  • It is on the de Havilland campus, so it is easy to fit in between lectures
  • There are student memberships just for UH students
  • Facilities include a gym, pool, sports halls and a climbing wall
  • Our top tip: book a tour if you are not sure where to start
Visit website

Reviewed by the ActiveHeartz team

item.title: Westminster Lodge: Swim and Train in St Albans
item.dc:creator: ti25aai
item.content:encoded:
Westminster Lodge Leisure Centre sits on the edge of Verulamium Park in St Albans. It has swimming pools, a gym and a busy timetable of fitness classes, so it is a great all-in-one stop for a workout.

Why we recommend it

  • Pools, gym and classes under one roof
  • Right next to Verulamium Park for a run before or after
  • Modern, welcoming facilities

Quick info

  • Review by: Jacob Hall
  • Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐ (4/5)
  • Advantage: A welcoming leisure centre with swimming lessons, fitness facilities and activities for all ages.
  • Disadvantage: Some swimming sessions have limited spaces, so planning ahead is important.
  • Overall: Westminster Lodge is an enjoyable place to spend time and focus on personal fitness. It provides opportunities to learn new swimming skills, build confidence in the water and take part in regular exercise.

Good to know

  • It sits right next to Verulamium Park
  • There are pools, a gym and a busy class timetable
  • It can be busy at peak times, so booking helps
  • Our top tip: warm up with a jog around the park first
Visit website

Reviewed by the ActiveHeartz team

item.title: Try Something New with Active Students
item.dc:creator: ti25aai
item.content:encoded:
Active Students is the University of Hertfordshire's programme of casual sport and activity sessions. There is no pressure and no experience needed. You just turn up, have fun and meet new people.

Why we recommend it

  • Made for UH students, so it is friendly and relaxed
  • A great way to try new sports without committing
  • Easy way to make friends, especially in your first year

Quick info

  • Review by: Benjamin Allen
  • Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (5/5)
  • Advantage: Encourages students to participate in physical activities, build confidence and develop teamwork skills.
  • Disadvantage: Not all activities may suit everyone’s interests, and some sessions can clash with study schedules.
  • Overall: Active Students provides a useful opportunity to balance university life with physical activity. It encourages students to take breaks from studying, challenge themselves and become involved in sporting activities.

Good to know

  • Sessions are designed for UH students
  • No experience or special kit needed
  • A great way to meet people outside your course
  • Our top tip: try a different sport each week until you find your favourite
See the timetable

Reviewed by the ActiveHeartz team

item.title: Smash It at Comets Badminton
item.dc:creator: ti25aai
item.content:encoded:
Comets Badminton is a local club in Welwyn Hatfield. It is a fun, sociable way to improve your game and play regularly with others who love the sport.

Why we recommend it

  • Friendly club atmosphere
  • Regular games to keep you consistent
  • Good way to meet people outside of uni

Quick info

  • Review by: Alexander Green
  • Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐ (4/5)
  • Advantage: Great opportunity to practise badminton, develop reaction speed and enjoy competitive games.
  • Disadvantage: Playing for long periods can be tiring, especially for beginners.
  • Overall: Smash It at Comets Badminton is an enjoyable activity for anyone interested in improving their sporting abilities. It provides a chance to challenge yourself, learn new techniques and build confidence on the court.

Good to know

  • A local club with regular games
  • Good for people who already enjoy badminton
  • Contact the club to check times and availability
  • Our top tip: bring non-marking indoor trainers
Club details

Reviewed by the ActiveHeartz team

item.title: Book a Court at Hatfield Leisure Centre
item.dc:creator: ti25aai
item.content:encoded:
Hatfield Leisure Centre is a handy place to book a badminton court with friends. It is a simple, affordable way to get moving and have a laugh at the same time.

Why we recommend it

  • Easy to book courts with friends
  • Close to Hatfield town and the University
  • Great for a casual, social workout

Quick info

  • Review by: Samuel Adams
  • Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐ (4/5)
  • Advantage: Improves stamina, concentration and hand-eye coordination while providing an enjoyable indoor activity.
  • Disadvantage: Finding available courts can be difficult at peak times, and equipment may need to be brought along.
  • Overall: Playing badminton in Hatfield is a good way to enjoy sport without needing to be an expert. It offers a chance to compete against friends, practise different techniques and gradually improve your performance.

Good to know

  • Courts can be booked by the hour
  • A cheap activity when split between friends
  • Easy to reach from Hatfield town
  • Our top tip: book a regular weekly slot with friends
Book badminton

Reviewed by the ActiveHeartz team

item.title: Playing Football at the University
item.dc:creator: ti25aai
item.content:encoded:
Football is one of the easiest ways to stay active and make friends at Herts. You can join a University team, play casually through student sessions, or book a pitch with friends for five-a-side.

Why we recommend it

  • Options for every level, from beginner to competitive
  • Pitches available at the Hertfordshire Sports Village
  • A brilliant way to build friendships

Quick info

  • Review by: William Carter
  • Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (5/5)
  • Advantage: Great opportunities to practise passing, shooting and ball control while enjoying competitive games.
  • Disadvantage: Weather conditions can affect outdoor sessions, and pitches may become slippery after rain.
  • Overall: Football at the University of Hertfordshire is an enjoyable way to combine exercise with socialising. It allows students to challenge themselves, improve their techniques and develop a better understanding of the game.

Good to know

  • Options range from casual kickabouts to University teams
  • Pitches are available at the Hertfordshire Sports Village
  • Mixed abilities are welcome in casual games
  • Our top tip: go to the sports fair at the start of term to find teams
UH sport

Reviewed by the ActiveHeartz team

item.title: Move Your Body, Calm Your Mind
item.dc:creator: ti25aai
item.content:encoded:
Exercise is not only about fitness. A short walk in a park, a gentle yoga class or a run with friends can lower stress and help you sleep and focus better, especially around deadlines.

Why we recommend it

  • A 20-minute walk in Ellenbrook Fields or along the Alban Way can clear your head
  • Group sessions help you feel less alone
  • The University offers active wellbeing sessions for students

Quick info

  • Review by: Thomas Roberts
  • Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (5/5)
  • Advantage: Encourages a healthier lifestyle through relaxation techniques, stress management and positive thinking.
  • Disadvantage: Mindfulness activities may take time to get used to, especially for students who are new to meditation.
  • Overall: Mental health and mindfulness at the University of Hertfordshire provide students with an opportunity to focus on their personal wellbeing. Taking part in these activities can help students understand their emotions, deal with everyday challenges and create better routines.

Good to know

  • Even short bursts of movement can lift your mood
  • Green spaces near campus are great for switching off
  • Moving with friends helps you feel more connected
  • Our top tip: schedule a short walk into every study day
Active Wellbeing

Reviewed by the ActiveHeartz team

item.title: Support from UH Student Wellbeing
item.dc:creator: ti25aai
item.content:encoded:
If you are struggling, you do not have to deal with it alone. The University of Hertfordshire offers free, confidential wellbeing support for students, alongside activities that help you look after your mental health.

Why we recommend it

  • Free and confidential for UH students
  • Friendly staff who understand student life
  • Works well alongside staying active

Quick info

  • Review by: Jack Turner
  • Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (5/5)
  • Advantage: Helps students access advice, develop independence and find support when facing personal or academic difficulties.
  • Disadvantage: It can sometimes be difficult to know which support service is best for a particular problem.
  • Overall: The University of Hertfordshire’s student wellbeing support is a useful resource for students adjusting to university life. It gives students opportunities to discuss concerns, access helpful guidance and find ways to overcome challenges.

Good to know

  • Support is free and confidential for UH students
  • You can reach out about small worries as well as big ones
  • They can point you to other services if needed
  • Our top tip: save their contact details now, before you need them

Reviewed by the ActiveHeartz team

item.title: Find Your Calm with Yoga and Pilates
item.dc:creator: ti25aai
item.content:encoded:
Yoga and Pilates are great for building strength, flexibility and focus. They are beginner friendly, low impact and a lovely way to switch off from studying.

Why we recommend it

  • Gentle on the body and good for posture after long study sessions
  • Classes available at the Hertfordshire Sports Village and local leisure centres
  • Helps reduce stress and improve sleep

Quick info

  • Review by: Leo Collins
  • Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (5/5)
  • Advantage: Encourages relaxation, strengthens core muscles and helps improve breathing and body awareness.
  • Disadvantage: Some classes require previous booking, and certain positions may take practice to master.
  • Overall: Yoga and Pilates offer a refreshing way to stay active without doing high-intensity exercise. They allow participants to work at their own pace while developing strength, improving posture and learning useful relaxation techniques.

Good to know

  • Classes suit all levels, including complete beginners
  • Great for posture after long study sessions
  • Helps with stress and sleep
  • Our top tip: tell the instructor if it is your first class
Visit website

Reviewed by the ActiveHeartz team

item.title: Get Active for Free in Hertfordshire
item.dc:creator: ti25aai
item.content:encoded:
You do not need money to get fit. Hertfordshire is full of free parks, trails and community events, perfect for students on a budget.

Why we recommend it

  • Free weekly parkrun 5k events across Hertfordshire
  • Free parks like Ellenbrook Fields and Verulamium Park
  • The Alban Way for free walking and cycling

Quick info

  • Review by: Ryan Morris
  • Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (5/5)
  • Advantage: Allows students to enjoy campus facilities, join community activities and discover new hobbies at little or no cost.
  • Disadvantage: The choice of free activities can vary throughout the academic year, so some opportunities may not always be available.
  • Overall: The free activities at the University of Hertfordshire are a useful way to make the most of student life. They give students the chance to explore different interests, become involved in campus life and spend time with others without needing a large budget.

Good to know

  • Parks and trails near campus are free all year round
  • Free parkrun events take place every weekend
  • No membership or equipment needed
  • Our top tip: invite a friend to keep each other motivated
Find a parkrun

Reviewed by the ActiveHeartz team

item.title: Pay As You Go: Train Without a Contract
item.dc:creator: ti25aai
item.content:encoded:
Pay-as-you-go lets you use a gym or pool only when you want to, with no monthly fee. It is perfect if your timetable changes every week or you are still working out what you enjoy.

Why we recommend it

  • No long-term contract
  • Only pay for the sessions you use
  • Try different gyms before choosing one

Quick info

  • Review by: Adam Richardson
  • Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐ (4/5)
  • Advantage: Easy access to different leisure activities, affordable single sessions and no long-term membership required.
  • Disadvantage: Prices can vary depending on the facility, and popular sessions may need to be booked in advance.
  • Overall: Pay-as-you-go options around the University of Hertfordshire are ideal for students who prefer having control over their spending. They make it easier to try different sports, attend fitness sessions and explore new activities without paying for a full membership.

Good to know

  • No contract or monthly commitment
  • Perfect for trying out different gyms
  • Can work out more expensive if you go very often
  • Our top tip: keep track of your visits for the first month
Find PAYG gyms

Reviewed by the ActiveHeartz team

item.title: Save Money with Student Discounts
item.dc:creator: ti25aai
item.content:encoded:
Being a student comes with perks. Many gyms and sports centres near the University offer cheaper memberships for students, so always bring your student ID.

Why we recommend it

  • UH student memberships at the Hertfordshire Sports Village
  • Many local leisure centres offer student or concession prices
  • Ask about free trials before you sign up

Quick info

  • Review by: Dylan Bell
  • Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (5/5)
  • Tip: Always carry your student ID
  • Advantage: Helps students save money on fitness memberships while making it easier to access modern gym equipment and exercise classes.
  • Disadvantage: Student offers may have age restrictions, limited availability or specific membership conditions.
  • Overall: Gym discounts for students around Hertfordshire are a great incentive to make exercise part of everyday life. They make joining a gym more manageable for students who need to balance fitness with other expenses.

Good to know

  • Most places need proof that you are a student
  • Discounts can save a lot over a year
  • Look out for offers at the start of each term
  • Our top tip: always ask, even if a discount is not advertised
UH memberships

Reviewed by the ActiveHeartz team

item.title: An Easy 5k Run at Ellenbrook Fields
item.dc:creator: ti25aai
item.content:encoded:
If you have been meaning to start running, Ellenbrook Fields is one of the easiest places near campus to do it. The wide, open paths mean you can find your own pace without dodging traffic or crowds.

What to expect

Expect long, gentle paths through grassland with big skies and very few hills. It is quiet on weekday mornings, and on weekends you will see other runners and dog walkers. After heavy rain some paths get muddy, so it feels more like a trail run.

Our tips

  • Wear shoes with a bit of grip in autumn and winter
  • There is not much shade, so bring water on warm days
  • Try a free weekend parkrun if you like running with others

Quick info

  • Review by: Amelia Brown
  • Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐ (4/5)
  • Advantage: Wide, flat paths with plenty of open space, ideal for walking, jogging and running.
  • Disadvantage: Some paths can become muddy after heavy rain, and there is limited shade on sunny days.
  • Overall: Ellenbrook Fields is a lovely, free outdoor space with peaceful scenery. It is great for beginners, regular runners and dog walkers.
  • Level: Beginner to intermediate

Reviewed by the ActiveHeartz team

item.title: The Alban Way on a Grey Day
item.dc:creator: ti25aai
item.content:encoded:
The Alban Way is lovely in the sunshine, but it is also a great option when the weather is not perfect. The trees along the old railway line give some shelter, and the flat route means you can keep moving without much effort.

What to expect

Expect a quiet, tree-lined path that feels calm even in drizzle. Some sections can collect puddles and leaves in autumn, so it is a little slower going. Bikes and walkers share the path, so it is friendly but you need to keep an eye out.

Our tips

  • Wear a waterproof and shoes you do not mind getting wet
  • Cyclists: ring your bell when passing walkers
  • Plan a short loop and turn back when you are ready

Quick info

  • Olivia Smith review:
  • Rating: ⭐⭐⭐ (3/5)
  • Advantage: Flat, peaceful and surrounded by trees making it great for walking and cycling
  • Disadvantage: Some sections can become muddy in wet weather and walkers share the same path
  • Overall: The Alban Way is a lovely, free route which offers beautiful scenery also it is a great place to enjoy fresh air and exercise
  • Level: Beginner

Reviewed by the ActiveHeartz team

item.title: Trying Paddleboarding at Stanborough Park
item.dc:creator: ti25aai
item.content:encoded:
If you fancy trying something completely new, the water sports centre at Stanborough Park is a fun place to start. Paddleboarding and sailing are great for balance and core strength, and they feel more like an adventure than a workout.

What to expect

Expect a short safety briefing before you get on the water, and probably a few wobbles at the start. The lake is calm and sheltered, which makes it beginner friendly. Sessions are seasonal and popular in summer, so it is worth checking times before you go.

Our tips

  • Book ahead in summer, especially at weekends
  • Bring a change of clothes and a towel
  • Go with a friend, it is much more fun when you both fall in!

Quick info

  • Review by: Sophia Taylor
  • Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐ (4/5)
  • Advantage: Lovely lakeside views, walking paths and plenty of outdoor activities.
  • Disadvantage: Can become busy at weekends, especially during warmer weather
  • Overall: Stanborough Park is a great place to enjoy the outdoors, with beautiful lakes and peaceful scenery. It is ideal for walking, cycling and spending time with friends or family.

Reviewed by the ActiveHeartz team

item.title: A Weekend Day Out at Verulamium Park
item.dc:creator: ti25aai
item.content:encoded:
Verulamium Park is perfect when you want exercise that does not feel like exercise. You can easily spend a whole afternoon walking around the lake, exploring the Roman remains and finishing in St Albans for food.

What to expect

Expect wide open lawns, a big lake with plenty of birds and lots of paths to explore. It gets busy on sunny weekends, which gives it a lively, friendly atmosphere. Cafés and the city centre are close by when you need a break.

Our tips

  • Combine a lake loop with a walk up into St Albans
  • Pack a picnic on warm days
  • Go early on weekends if you prefer it quieter

Quick info

  • Review by: Isabella Wilson
  • Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (5/5)
  • Advantage: Beautiful historic surroundings, large green spaces and peaceful walking trails.
  • Disadvantage: Some areas can become crowded during weekends and holidays.
  • Overall: Verulamium Park is a wonderful place to explore, with a mixture of history, nature and open spaces. It is perfect for relaxing walks, picnics and outdoor activities.
  • Level: Everyone

Reviewed by the ActiveHeartz team

item.title: Gosling Sports Park With Your Friends
item.dc:creator: ti25aai
item.content:encoded:
Gosling Sports Park is a brilliant choice for a group day out. With so many activities on one site, everyone can find something they enjoy, from the gym to racket sports and the trampoline park.

What to expect

Expect a big, busy centre with lots going on. It is easy to fill a couple of hours trying different things. Some activities need booking, and the popular ones fill up at evenings and weekends.

Our tips

  • Book group activities in advance
  • Check the timetable for student-friendly times
  • Make it a social: plan food together afterwards

Quick info

  • Review by: Mia Robinson
  • Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐ (4/5)
  • Advantage: Excellent sports facilities, spacious grounds and a wide range of activities.
  • Disadvantage: Some facilities can be busy during peak hours, especially after school and at weekends.
    Overall: Gosling Sports Park is a great place for keeping active and trying different sports. It offers plenty of opportunities for exercise, whether you enjoy swimming, tennis, athletics or using the gym.
  • Level: Everyone

Reviewed by the ActiveHeartz team

item.title: Swimming for Beginners at Hatfield Swim Centre
item.dc:creator: ti25aai
item.content:encoded:
Not a confident swimmer? Hatfield Swim Centre is a relaxed place to build up your confidence in the water. Swimming is low impact and great for both fitness and stress relief.

What to expect

Expect lane swimming sessions split by speed, so you can stay in the slow lane without feeling rushed. Off-peak times tend to be calmer. The changing rooms are straightforward and the centre is easy to get to from Hatfield town.

Our tips

  • Start with short sessions and build up
  • Look for quieter off-peak times on the timetable
  • Ask reception about adult swimming lessons

Quick info

  • Review by: Emily White
  • Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐ (4/5)
  • Advantage: Good swimming facilities, helpful staff and activities suitable for different ages.
  • Disadvantage: The pool can become crowded during evenings and weekends.
  • Overall: Hatfield Swim Centre is a great place to enjoy swimming and improve fitness. It offers a welcoming environment for beginners and more experienced swimmers.
  • Level: Beginner to advanced

Reviewed by the ActiveHeartz team

item.title: Your First Climb at the Sports Village
item.dc:creator: ti25aai
item.content:encoded:
The climbing wall at the Hertfordshire Sports Village is one of the best-kept secrets on campus. Climbing works your whole body and your problem-solving skills at the same time, and it is really satisfying when you reach the top.

What to expect

Expect a friendly, supportive atmosphere where beginners are welcome. You will usually need an induction or taster session first so you learn the safety basics. After that, it is a fun way to spend an evening with friends.

Our tips

  • Ask about taster or induction sessions first
  • Wear comfortable clothes you can stretch in
  • Go with a friend so you can take turns

Quick info

  • Review by: Grace Martin
  • Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (5/5)
  • Advantage: Modern gym equipment, a large swimming pool and a variety of fitness and sports activities.
  • Disadvantage: Membership and activity costs can be quite expensive, especially for regular visitors.
  • Overall: Hertfordshire Sports Village is a great place for people who enjoy keeping fit and trying different activities. It offers a range of facilities, including swimming, gym workouts and sports sessions.
  • Level: Beginner friendly

Reviewed by the ActiveHeartz team

item.title: Fitness Classes at Westminster Lodge
item.dc:creator: ti25aai
item.content:encoded:
Westminster Lodge has a busy timetable of fitness classes, which is great if you work out better with an instructor and a group. It is a good option if you live in or near St Albans.

What to expect

Expect energetic classes and a modern studio. Because it is popular, peak-time classes can fill up and the centre can feel busy in the evenings. Booking ahead makes it much easier.

Our tips

  • Book classes in advance, especially evenings
  • Arrive a few minutes early for your first class
  • Try a quieter daytime class if your timetable allows

Quick info

  • Review by: Charlotte Lewis
  • Rating: ⭐⭐⭐ (3/5)
    Advantage:     Good swimming facilities, a well-equipped gym and a variety of fitness classes.
  • Disadvantage: The swimming pool and gym can become crowded during peak hours.
  • Overall: Westminster Lodge is a great leisure centre for people who want to stay active and improve their fitness. It offers a good combination of swimming, gym workouts and exercise classes.
  • Level: Beginner to intermediate

Reviewed by the ActiveHeartz team

item.title: Making Friends Through Active Students
item.dc:creator: ti25aai
item.content:encoded:
Moving to university can feel lonely at first, and Active Students sessions are one of the easiest ways to meet people. The focus is on having fun, not on being good at sport.

What to expect

Expect relaxed, welcoming sessions where lots of people are trying something for the first time. You do not need any kit beyond comfortable clothes and trainers, and there is no pressure to come every week.

Our tips

  • Check the timetable and pick one session to try
  • Bring a flatmate if you feel nervous going alone
  • Try a sport you have never played before

Quick info

  • Review by: Ava Young
  • Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (5/5)
  • Advantage: A welcoming leisure centre with swimming lessons, fitness facilities and activities for all ages.
  • Disadvantage: Some swimming sessions have limited spaces, so planning ahead is important.
  • Overall: Westminster Lodge is an enjoyable place to spend time and focus on personal fitness. It provides opportunities to learn new swimming skills, build confidence in the water and take part in regular exercise.

Reviewed by the ActiveHeartz team

item.title: Your First Night at Comets Badminton
item.dc:creator: ti25aai
item.content:encoded:
Joining a club can feel a bit daunting, but Comets Badminton is a good step up if you already enjoy playing casually and want regular games.

What to expect

Expect friendly, competitive games with players of mixed ability. As a club, it suits people who can commit to coming regularly. It is worth contacting the club first to check times and whether there is a space for new players.

Our tips

  • Contact the club before your first visit
  • Bring non-marking indoor trainers
  • Be ready to play doubles with new people

Quick info

  • Review by: Lily Scott
  • Rating: ⭐⭐⭐ (3/5)
  • Advantage: Fun badminton sessions, opportunities to improve skills and a great way to stay active.
  • Disadvantage: Courts can become busy during popular sessions, and booking ahead may be necessary.
  • Overall: Smash It at Comets Badminton is a great place for anyone who enjoys racket sports or wants to try something new. It provides an opportunity to practise techniques, improve coordination and enjoy friendly competition.
  • Level: Some experience helps

Reviewed by the ActiveHeartz team

item.title: A Cheap Night Out: Badminton in Hatfield
item.dc:creator: ti25aai
item.content:encoded:
Looking for something different to do with friends? Booking a badminton court at Hatfield Leisure Centre is cheap, social and a surprisingly good workout.

What to expect

Expect simple, well-kept courts that you can book by the hour. Split between friends, it is an affordable evening. Rackets and shuttlecocks may be available, but it is worth checking before you go.

Our tips

  • Split the court cost between four people
  • Check if you need to bring your own rackets
  • Book evening slots a few days ahead

Quick info

  • Review by: Chloe Baker
  • Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐ (4/5)
  • Advantage: A fun way to improve fitness, practise badminton skills and enjoy friendly matches.
  • Disadvantage: Court availability can be limited during busy evenings and weekends.
  • Overall: Badminton in Hatfield is a great activity for people who enjoy sports and staying active. It helps improve speed, balance and coordination while providing an opportunity to meet other players.
  • Level: Everyone

Reviewed by the ActiveHeartz team

item.title: Five-a-Side With Your Flatmates
item.dc:creator: ti25aai
item.content:encoded:
You do not need to be on a team to enjoy football at uni. Booking a five-a-side pitch with flatmates is a great way to keep fit and bond at the same time.

What to expect

Expect fast, fun games where everyone gets plenty of touches of the ball. Evening slots are the most popular, so book in advance. It is casual, so mixed abilities are completely fine.

Our tips

  • Get a regular weekly slot so it becomes a habit
  • Split the pitch cost between everyone
  • Bring water and a spare top

Quick info

  • Review by: Ella Nelson
  • Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐ (4/5)
  • Advantage: Large playing areas, opportunities to develop football skills and a great environment for team sports.
  • Disadvantage: Pitch availability can be limited, especially when university teams are training or playing matches.
  • Overall: Playing football at the University of Hertfordshire is a great way to stay active and enjoy being part of a team. It helps improve fitness, communication and teamwork while allowing players to develop their football abilities.
  • Level: Everyone

Reviewed by the ActiveHeartz team

item.title: Beat Exam Stress With a 20-Minute Walk
item.dc:creator: ti25aai
item.content:encoded:
When deadlines pile up, it is tempting to stay at your desk. But a short walk outside is one of the simplest ways to reset your mind, and you will often come back more focused.

What to expect

Expect to feel calmer and clearer after just 20 minutes. Places like Ellenbrook Fields and the Alban Way are close to campus and quiet enough to really switch off.

Our tips

  • Leave your headphones out for once and notice your surroundings
  • Walk with a friend and agree not to talk about exams
  • Make it a daily habit during revision season

Quick info

  • Review by: Freya Mitchell
  • Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (5/5)
  • Advantage: Provides a chance to relax, manage stress and develop positive habits through mindfulness activities.
  • Disadvantage: Finding time to attend sessions can be difficult alongside lectures, assignments and other university commitments.
  • Overall: Mental health and mindfulness activities at the University of Hertfordshire are a valuable way for students to take a break from busy university life. They encourage relaxation, self-awareness and a more positive mindset.
  • Level: Everyone

Reviewed by the ActiveHeartz team

item.title: When to Reach Out to Student Wellbeing
item.dc:creator: ti25aai
item.content:encoded:
Lots of students wait until things feel really bad before asking for help. You do not need to. The University's Student Wellbeing team is there for small worries as well as big ones.

What to expect

Expect friendly, confidential support from people who understand student life. They can help you talk things through and point you towards other support if you need it.

Our tips

  • You can reach out about stress, homesickness or anything else
  • Look up Student Wellbeing on Ask Herts to find out how to get in touch
  • Combine support with small healthy habits, like a daily walk

Quick info

  • Review by: Ruby Philips
  • Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (5/5)
  • Advantage: Offers guidance, support services and activities that help students feel included and supported
  • Disadvantage: Some support services may have waiting times, particularly during busy academic periods.
  • Overall: Student wellbeing at the University of Hertfordshire plays an important role in helping students enjoy university life. The support available encourages students to look after themselves, build confidence and manage challenges both inside and outside the classroom.
  • Level: Open to all students

Reviewed by the ActiveHeartz team

item.title: Yoga for Complete Beginners
item.dc:creator: ti25aai
item.content:encoded:
If you spend hours hunched over a laptop, yoga is a brilliant way to undo some of the stiffness. It is gentle, calming and suitable for any fitness level.

What to expect

Expect slow, guided movements and lots of focus on breathing. Instructors usually offer easier versions of each pose, so nobody is left behind. Do not worry if you cannot touch your toes, most people cannot at first!

Our tips

  • Tell the instructor it is your first class
  • Wear comfortable, stretchy clothes
  • Go regularly for a few weeks to really feel the difference

Quick info

  • Review by: Evie Parker
  • Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐ (4/5)
  • Advantage: Helps improve flexibility, balance and posture while reducing stress and building strength.
  • Disadvantage: Some exercises can be challenging for beginners, and classes may have limited spaces.
  • Overall: Yoga and Pilates are excellent activities for improving both physical and mental wellbeing. They provide a relaxing environment to focus on movement, breathing and strength. Taking part in regular sessions can help improve flexibility, reduce tension and develop better body control.
  • Level: Complete beginners

Reviewed by the ActiveHeartz team

item.title: Five Free Ways to Get Active This Week
item.dc:creator: ti25aai
item.content:encoded:
Staying active does not have to cost anything. Here are five free ideas you can try around Hatfield this week.

What to expect

Expect fresh air, a bit of effort and zero cost. These ideas work whether you have ten minutes or a whole afternoon.

Our tips

  • Join a free weekend parkrun 5k
  • Walk or jog a loop of Ellenbrook Fields
  • Cycle part of the Alban Way
  • Do a bodyweight workout in a local park
  • Organise a kickabout with friends on a free pitch

Quick info

  • Review by: Hannah Edwards
  • Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (5/5)
  • Advantage: Plenty of opportunities to socialise, explore the campus and take part in activities without spending money.
  • Disadvantage: Some free activities are only available at certain times or during specific university events.
  • Overall: Free activities at the University of Hertfordshire are a great way for students to enjoy university life without worrying about extra costs. They provide opportunities to meet new people, discover new interests and take part in enjoyable experiences outside of lectures.
  • Level: Everyone

Reviewed by the ActiveHeartz team

item.title: Is Pay As You Go Right for You?
item.dc:creator: ti25aai
item.content:encoded:
Pay-as-you-go is a great way to try gyms and pools without signing a contract. But depending on how often you go, it is not always the cheapest option.

What to expect

Expect total flexibility: you pay for each visit and there is nothing to cancel. If you end up going several times a week, a monthly membership may work out cheaper, so it is worth keeping track.

Our tips

  • Use pay-as-you-go to try a few places first
  • Count your visits after a month and compare costs
  • Look out for student or off-peak prices

Quick info

  • Review by: Jessica Cooper
  • Rating: ⭐⭐⭐ (3/5)
  • Advantage: Flexible access to sports and fitness facilities without needing to commit to a monthly membership.
  • Disadvantage: Regular visits can become expensive, and some activities require additional booking fees.
  • Overall: Pay-as-you-go activities near the University of Hertfordshire are a convenient option for students who want to stay active while managing their budgets. They allow students to choose when they exercise and only pay for the sessions they attend.
  • Level: Everyone

Reviewed by the ActiveHeartz team

item.title: How to Get the Most From Student Discounts
item.dc:creator: ti25aai
item.content:encoded:
Student discounts can save you a lot over a year, but only if you remember to use them. Here is how to make the most of them.

What to expect

Expect most local gyms and leisure centres to offer some kind of student or concession price. You will usually need to show proof that you are a student.

Our tips

  • Always carry your student ID
  • Ask about student prices before signing up anywhere
  • Look out for free trials and taster sessions at the start of term

Quick info

  • Review by: Megan Bailey
  • Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐ (4/5)
  • Advantage: Reduced membership prices, affordable fitness options and access to gym facilities at a lower cost for students.
  • Disadvantage: Some discounts may only apply to selected memberships or require valid student identification.
  • Overall: Student discounts at gyms near the University of Hertfordshire are a great way to make fitness more affordable. They allow students to access exercise equipment, fitness classes and other facilities while keeping their spending under control.
  • Level: Everyone

Reviewed by the ActiveHeartz team
